content.title: Royal Caribbean dials up sailings from China
content.text: Royal Caribbean is ramping up its commitment to the China market with an enhanced slew of East Asia itineraries, for its 2027-28 season on Spectrum of the Seas.The ship will sail across 22 destinations, offering a range of three- to 11-night getaways, covering China, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam.“This new lineup reflects our continued commitment to the China market and our ambition to deliver more diverse and immersive vacations,” said Benjamin Bouldin, president, Royal Caribbean, Greater China.Additionally, these sailings are lengthier now, appealing to Chinese vacationers who are “seeking deeper connections with loved ones”. A highlight is the eight- to 10-night trip from Shanghai, Tokyo and Hong Kong, where for the first time, guests can sail one way between cities – starting or ending their journey in Tokyo.Options have been timed to capture specific seasons.The spring season in May 2027 sails across China, Japan and South Korea, capturing the region’s spring bloom season – from Beijing’s peonies to Fukuoka’s wisteria in Japan and Jeju’s hydrangeas. It will also be possible to extend two overnight stays in North China’s Beijing (Tianjin).October 2027 will focus on autumn foliage to Seoul (Incheon), South Korea, and Sapporo (Muroran), Japan. Extensions can be made for eight nights in the popular Osaka and Tokyo.Alternatively, passengers looking for shorter escapes and weekend trips can depart from Shanghai and Hong Kong on 3-4 night sailings to Jeju and Busan, or 5-8 night sailings to Tokyo, Osaka, Seoul, Busan and Jeju.Festive sailings are also part of the enhanced East Asia offerings.Guests can choose from three holiday getaways during Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year, on five-, nine- or 11-night sailings to popular stops including Fukuoka, Okinawa, Kagoshima, Busan and Jeju. The adventures also feature activities, such as whale watching and the chance to spot early cherry blossoms.The Hong Kong will also expand access to Hue and Da Nang (Chan May) in Vietnam.Bookings are now open.
